chapter: Writing, Oklahoma roots and the origins of bebop
title: Prez, Hawkins and 'Body and Soul'
summary: McGhee followed Prez nightly and praised Hawkins' 'Body and Soul' nights.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Yeah, well, he was something else. But he sounded so beautiful, man, I don't know how anybody wouldn't want to do something for him, man. I remember I used to love to go... I used to go and hear that sound that was coming out of Minton's when Charlie would be there playing. Prez, too. I had to go out with Prez damn near every night. Even when he was with Basie and I was with Barnet, I'd still go out with him every night. Because he just sounded so good, man.
You just wanted to be around that sound.

Yeah. Well, you know, that's where it was at. I know Billie Holiday loved his sound, because every time I'd look up, I'd see here, wherever I'd go. So I know she loved the sound. I guess all the guys really dug it.
Of course, Prez having the kind of ear he had and the kind of ideas he had, definitely was one of the people who led into the so-called new music of Bebop.
And yet he wasn't really playing in that style, although later he kind of incorporated parts of it...
But in the Minton's days, he wasn't really playing in
that kind of style. But it fit, because he was already...

Yeah, he sounded good. Whatever he was playing, it was good. I won't say it was the greatest thing in the world, but I didn't know anybody that sounded any better. And that even includes Coleman Hawkins and everybody else, and everybody was so wrapped up in Hawk... When Hawk came back here, I think he did a wonderful thing on "Body and Soul." I don't think nobody ever played any more "Body and Soul" than Hawk did. I used to hear him play it every night, so I heard it all kind of ways -- on his off nights, on his good nights, etcetera. So I know how he did to "Body and Soul." But Prez was taking care of business, too, you know.

Of course. You were talking before about the way Charlie Christian ended "Solo Flight," and you said that you had been playing and other people had been playing that figure, but it was the way he did it...
Yeah, the way he did it that made it come out.
